proposals: The Labour Bureau should publish a back-cast of the rural wage series on the new 787-village, 34-state sampling frame, so the July 2025 break can be measured officially rather than by an outside analyst’s splice of roughly 4.3 per cent.

The Labour Bureau should print a dated break note on every wage-rate and CPI-AL/CPI-RL table issued since July 2025, stating that the sample changed from 600 to 787 villages, so the 17–18 per cent headline is not read as a pay rise.

The Labour Bureau should publish, for a full overlap year, CPI-AL computed with both arithmetic and geometric means, so the Ministry of Rural Development and states can see how much of the 1.42 per cent June 2025 inflation print comes from the averaging change alone.

The Ministry of Rural Development should state, in each wage notification under VB-G RAM G, the index series, base and weighting used to set the rate, and say whether its national average is simple or weighted, so the ₹370 and ₹298.8 figures can be reconciled.

The Labour Bureau should publish state-wise wage and price series with each state’s sample-village weight alongside its Census rural-population share, so users can re-weight the national average themselves when newly added regions hold about 11 per cent of villages but 1.15 per cent of rural population.
